extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB) inter partes proceedings (including pro se litigants)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practical guidance for disclosures and discovery in inter partes proceedings before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, covering discovery conferences, initial disclosures, expert disclosures, timing, scope, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Federal Rules to Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever appropriate, the provisions of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure relating to disclosure and discovery shall apply in opposition, cancellation, interference and concurrent use registration proceedings except as otherwise provided; discovery before the Board under 37 CFR § 2.120 is similar in many respects to discovery before the federal district courts, but in modified form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Fed. R. Civ. P. discovery rules as applicable to Board proceedings except where 37 CFR § 2.120 or the Board's orders provide otherwise. See specific TBMP provisions for modifications (e.g., timing, required disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board-specified discovery schedule and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will specify the deadline for a discovery conference, the opening and closing dates for the taking of discovery, and the deadlines within the discovery period for making initial disclosures and expert disclosure; these dates are set in the trial order included with the notice of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the trial order's dates; if pleadings change (default, Rule 12 motion, counterclaim), the Board will reset deadlines. Parties seeking alterations must obtain Board approval or stipulation approved by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory discovery conference (post-November 1, 2007 cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inter partes proceedings commenced on or after November 1, 2007, parties are obliged to conduct a discovery conference to discuss disclosure and discovery plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference must occur no later than the opening of the discovery period; obligations include discussing matters in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f) and those in the institution order. Mere settlement discussion does not substitute for a full conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required subjects for discovery conference
rubrics_metrics.description: The discovery conference shall discuss the subjects set forth in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f) and any subjects set forth in the Board's institution order, including nature/basis of claims and defenses, settlement possibilities, preservation of discoverable information, and arrangements relating to disclosures, discovery, and introduction of evidence at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also discuss ACR, mediation/arbitration options, whether to alter disclosure or discovery procedures (including the Standard Protective Order), limitations on discovery, and stipulations to facilitate introduction of discovery materials at trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board participation in discovery conference
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board Interlocutory Attorney or Administrative Trademark Judge will participate in the conference upon request of any party made after answer but no later than ten days prior to the deadline for the conference; the participating attorney/judge may expand or reduce subjects to be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request Board participation via telephone or ESTTA no later than 10 days before the conference deadline; Board participation is by phone and is encouraged where pro se litigants are involved or parties are at an impasse (Board may allow participation with less than ten days' notice in such cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to file discovery plan/report
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the Federal Rules, parties do not have to file a disclosure/discovery plan with the Board following their discovery conference unless seeking leave to alter deadlines/obligations or directed by the Board to file such a report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties stipulate to alter discovery obligations, the stipulation must be approved by the Board to be effective; otherwise the Board will assume compliance with its rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: When discovery conference obligation is stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to have a discovery conference is effectively stayed where the defendant is in default, a Rule 12 pleading motion has been filed, or a counterclaim has been filed, because an answer must be filed before a meaningful conference can occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will reset the discovery conference deadline and subsequent dates upon resolution of the default/Rule 12 motion/acknowledgement of the counterclaim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial disclosures must be made no later than thirty days after the opening of the discovery period (per 37 CFR § 2.120(a)(2) / TBMP guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party generally must make initial disclosures prior to seeking traditional discovery devices unless modified by stipulation approved by the Board or by Board order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precondition to seeking discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must make its initial disclosures prior to seeking discovery, absent modification by stipulation approved by the Board, a motion granted by the Board, or Board order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party objects to discovery on the basis that required initial disclosures were not made, that objection must be specifically articulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of initial disclosures — witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must provide the name and, if known, the address and telephone number of each individual likely to have discoverable information — along with the subjects of that information — that the disclosing party may use to support its claims or defenses (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1)(A)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every possible witness must be listed — only those likely to have discoverable information the party may use to support claims/defenses. If a trial witness is identified, provide subject matter and known contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of initial disclosures — documents and ESI
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must provide a copy — or a description by category and location — of all documents, electronically stored information, and tangible things that the disclosing party has in its possession, custody, or control and may use to support its claims or defenses (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1)(A)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may either identify location or produce copies; the Board encourages actual exchange of copies rather than merely identifying location. ESI must be identified in initial disclosures where pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures are not exhaustive; standard for disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial disclosures are intended to prompt routine disclosure of names of potential witnesses and basic information about documents and things that a party may use to support a claim or defense, not to substitute for all discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party need not identify every witness/document that may have discoverable information, only those it may use to support claims/defenses. Nevertheless, parties may stipulate (with Board approval) to rely on reciprocal disclosures in lieu of formal discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures treated like discovery responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial written disclosures and initial disclosures of documents are treated like responses to discovery requests in that they may be used in support of or in opposition to a motion for summary judgment and may, at trial, be introduced by notice of reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume initial disclosures are informal — they can be used substantively; ensure accuracy and timely supplementation as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to supplement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a continuing duty to supplement initial disclosures and discovery responses as required under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must timely supplement when new information arises. Failure to supplement can lead to motions to compel, exclusion of evidence, or sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing to make initial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A party failing to make initial disclosures may be subject to a motion to compel and ultimately, a motion for discovery sanctions; a party may not file a motion for summary judgment until it has made its initial disclosures (with limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include compel orders and sanctions; summary judgment motions (except those asserting claim/issue preclusion or lack of Board jurisdiction) are premature until initial disclosures are served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert disclosures governed by Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of expert testimony must occur in the manner and sequence provided in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2), unless alternate directions have been provided by the Board in an institution or subsequent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must follow Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2) content and timing requirements unless the Board orders otherwise; expert disclosure deadlines in Board cases are typically set (TBMP notes expert disclosure is due 30 days prior to the close of discovery unless otherwise ordered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert report requirements for retained experts
rubrics_metrics.description: When a testifying expert is retained or specially employed, the disclosure must be accompanied by a written report prepared and signed by the witness, containing: (i) complete statement of opinions and basis, (ii) facts/data considered, (iii) exhibits to summarize/support opinions, (iv) qualifications including publications in prior 10 years, (v) list of other cases in prior 4 years where testified, and (vi) compensation statement (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide a proper report can lead to exclusion of expert testimony; ensure reports are thorough and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure for unretained experts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the witness is not required to provide a written report (e.g., unretained expert), the disclosure must state the subject matter on which the witness is expected to present evidence and a summary of the facts and opinions to which the witness is expected to testify (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2)(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient summary to allow opposing parties to determine need for rebuttal experts and to pursue expert discovery; consult the Board's orders on the scope of required disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, late retention, and motions for leave to use experts
rubrics_metrics.description: If an expert is retained after the deadline for disclosure of expert testimony, the party must promptly file a motion for leave to use expert testimony; prompt disclosure after the deadline does not guarantee the expert’s testimony will be allowed at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide within the discovery period whether to use an expert; if late, file motion for leave and be prepared to show good cause. The Board decides late-identification issues case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board notification and possible suspension for expert discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party disclosing plans to use an expert must notify the Board that it has made the required disclosure (but should not file with the Board copies of materials provided to adverse parties). The Board may then suspend proceedings to allow for discovery limited to experts and/or set deadlines for rebuttal experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify Board when experts are disclosed to facilitate scheduling; suspension orders can be limited to expert-related discovery, and the Board may or may not change other deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation regarding expert discovery and stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are expected to cooperate in exchanging information about testifying experts and should discuss, during the discovery conference, the possibility of entering into stipulations that will facilitate exchange of such information and/or the presentation of expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulate where possible to streamline expert discovery (e.g., exchange of CVs, agreed-upon dates for depositions), and revisit stipulations if experts become involved later in the case.
